resolution.note:
Both refuters killed every blocking finding, so the row stamps PASS:verify-refuted and this REVISE stays as the record. slides §4 (second failure, muted read; check_writing §28) line 4: harm: The rule match is real, but the finding does not hold up as BLOCKING. Checked: the file, `check_slides.md §4`, `check_writing.md §28`, the instance JSON, the host lecture and git history.

Facts the judge got right:
- L4 has three verbless fragments: "One more window." / "First prompt: *...*" / "Then the same dinner prompt."
- The reveal at L6 follows the setup.
- The maintainer block has no accept-note.

(a) Harm is tidiness, not a broken beat.
- Nothing is left to the trainer's finger. There is no screen deictic and no "take a guess before it runs".
- The setup quotes the exact prompt: *"I'm a cardiologist preparing dinner for my patients."* "The same dinner prompt" resolves on the preceding slide, `same-question-two-answers`, which uses "What should we have for dinner?" and "Same dinner question".
- A self-study reader in `claude-basics` gets all of this in text. The include order is cover, same-question, reads-whole, this slide, so the referent is on the page.
- This is not the canonical failure ("The same question, two answers. Two Claude Code sessions."), where the scene itself is missing.

(d) Another line carries the meaning. L6 ("The suggestion shifts: heart-healthy... You told the LLM who you are.") restates the whole scenario. L8 closes the beat. A reader loses nothing if L4 stays as is.

(e) The judge's baseline is partly wrong.
- It says the 2026-10-06 version "had verbed sentences". That is true only of the reveal paragraph.
- By `git show`, the 2026-10-06 setup was "One more window. The first prompt: *...*" plus "Then the same second prompt about dinner.", which is verbless in the same way.
- That version passed the slides judge at @b58bcc4c under the same §4, which carries the "Second failure (2026-09-13)" clause. Under the same rule text, the shape passed before and is now BLOCKING.
- The only change to the setup was commit 25c825e3, a deliberate language compaction pass that merged the two fragments. It did not introduce a new defect class.

(c) The fix has a cost. It re-expands a passage that the maintainer's compaction pass deliberately tightened. It is small, but it works against that direction for no reader benefit. The same pass also gave L6 its "LLM" wording.

BLOCKING severity is unwarranted for a slide whose scene a reader can fully reconstruct.
